title: Luel Speech is now available for public access
summary: Specialist production audio for unrepresented languages: eight voices across Tibetan, Darija, Masri and Dzongkha, in the Studio or over the API.
body_markdown:
## The voices


Two per language, each built from its own native-speaker corpus rather than a multilingual checkpoint borrowed from the language next door.


- **Dolma** and **Tenzin** —[Ü-Tsang Tibetan](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/tibetan-tts) , 48 kHz
- **Salma** and **Anir** —[Moroccan Darija](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/moroccan-darija-tts) , 24 kHz
- **Cleopatra** and **Mana** —[Egyptian Arabic (Masri)](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/masri-egyptian-tts) , 24 kHz
- **Pema** and **Jigme** —[Dzongkha](https://www.luel.ai/lab/models/dzongkha-emotive-tts) , 48 kHz


Ask for a slug that is not on that list and the call is refused rather than substituted. You never get a different voice than the one you named.


## The Luel Speech API


Every voice above, over one endpoint and one key. The official TypeScript SDK is` @luel/speech` .


```text
npm   install   @luel/speech
```


Name a voice, send the script it reads, and audio comes back:


```text
import   { Luel }   from   '@luel/speech'


const   luel   =   new   Luel  ({ apiKey: process.env.  LUEL_API_KEY  !   })


const   audio   =   await   luel.speech.  convert  ({
voice:   'bo-female'  ,
text:   'བཀྲ་ཤིས་བདེ་ལེགས།'  ,
})
```


[Quickstart](https://www.luel.ai/docs/speech/quickstart) ·[Voices](https://www.luel.ai/docs/speech/voices) ·[SDK reference](https://www.luel.ai/docs/speech/sdk)


Behind them is the engine the rest of[Luel Labs](https://www.luel.ai/blog/introducing-luel-lab) runs on: 750,000+ contributors across 96+ countries, recording the languages other platforms skip.
